memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational areas. The reference frame focuses on equitable participant compensation across burden, modality, iteration, and disruptions, while the compared frame focuses on research-plan traceability, preregistration, bounded targets, field risks, safety precedence, and proposal-authoring habits.

relations.reason: These memories state or support one reference-only basis for calculating fair compensation; the compared frame contains no corresponding compensation rule.
relations.summary: Participant compensation should reflect total participation burden, including session time, required preparation, and face-to-face travel.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule about compensation method availability.
relations.summary: Cash should remain an available payment method for face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule about when payment-method details must be settled.
relations.summary: A proposal need not finalize the payment method when compensation equity is adequately explained.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only policy governing rate equality across study modalities.
relations.summary: Face-to-face and remote studies should use the same base hourly rate when task burden is equal.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule addressing burdens created by multi-session iteration.
relations.summary: Compensation should account for rescheduling and repeated attendance in iterative formative evaluations.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule for compensating disrupted sessions.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for time already invested when prototype errors terminate a session early.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only observation about authoring behavior, distinct from the normative compensation policies.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to omit between-session preparation burden from iterative-study compensation calculations.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories split and justify one methodological requirement for an assessable, end-to-end data plan.
relations.summary: Each HCI research question should be traceable to specified data sources, collection tools and timing, and analysis procedures.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories specify complementary parts of one change-documentation policy.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should state both the criteria for judging plan changes and where those changes will be recorded.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories jointly state, elaborate, and justify one operational policy for meaningful target ranges.
relations.summary: When confirmations may change, use a justified bounded target whose minimum and maximum specify distinct deliverables, session and facilitator workload, schedule or cost consequences, and remaining uncertainty.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only caution about attributing failures in field deployments.
relations.summary: Field task failures may arise independently from network or service instability as well as from design choices.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only contingency policy for field safety events.
relations.summary: Institutional safety procedures take precedence over research schedules and data-collection plans when a field-system safety signal occurs.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only observation about proposal-authoring behavior.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance covers traceable data plans, preregistration changes, operationally meaningful target ranges, field-system failure attribution, safety precedence, and a tendency to frame feature lists as contributions.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance covers burden-based compensation, modality-neutral rates, payment-method flexibility, iterative and interrupted sessions, and a tendency to omit preparation effort.
